445: Unbelievable, but true. It's dangerous for you to stay in that getup.
446: Maybe tomorrow? It's still New Year, and in their own way they tried too.
447: We live out of town—it's unlikely the Docent can find us.
448:
All right, but don't step off the dacha for a second!
Also, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife—here's her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on the first, promise?
- We promise!
451:
Pity—such a good woman, and her father
is a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you out?
- He showed up... a bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year everything will be new for you.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
and I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... one moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? You can't make anything out
of him now.
459: What is there to make out? He says, wherever you are, I'll find you and slit your throat.
461:
They say he did Ryaboy with a razor—slice, and goodnight.
- He's gone completely rabid, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to see you? Santa Claus has come to see you,
he brought you presents!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. It's all ahead.
465:
- For now they'll come in handy in prison too. Wear them.
- All you know is to crow doom.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's boring without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could just sit, talk heart to heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor to have heart-to-heart talks with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Look at him! Found himself a sucker to play with!
You've got nine aces in the deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game—cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you, with the last letter "A"—Astrakhan.
And you, with "N"—Novgorod, get it?
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Good. And you, then—"A".
- Jambul. - What's Jambul got to do with it?
480:
Because it's warm there, that's my home,
that's my mom.
481:
Then let's play like this. I'll go out, you hide something,
I'll come back—find it.
482:
- You'd better find the helmet.
- Shut up.
483:
- We'll hide it and he'll watch through a hole?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you make sure I don't peek.
Why me? Anything happens—right away Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your jaws apart, you filthy little—
- Jaws, jaws...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a dad, a mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on your own.
- Oh, so you're here too.
491:
I was about to come to you, but I can feel
there's an ambush there.
492: Mityay, I need to lie low.
495:
- Sorry, doctor, for bothering you for nothing.
- It's fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Hello, dear Papa! We found out that
you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you had died."
501:
What bastard spilled the beans
to this little Khmyr about Khmyr?
502:
"And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came, she cried all day,
503:
and before that she said you were
a test pilot."
505:
"And I'm happy anyway that you're alive,
because Mom says
506: that you're a good man, but weak-willed."
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—stole the common money
and blamed it on the taxi driver.
508: Make tracks! I'll knock your horns off, radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed! You're forty years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What's behind you? What's in the present?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late. That's my advice.
513:
Hear me, Docent, we need to clear out:
That lady doctor will squeal to the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I did her—with a razor across the throat...
515: she's in the well, you can go take a look.
516: What did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let's say ten!
520: And for a lousy 14 years I have to put up with this viper?
521:
The one the old woman put in the well?
You do what you want, I'm going to the police.
523:
And you? You'll keep tolerating him
till death, huh?
524: Vasya, I told him earlier: I've got a runny nose—so he...
525:
Enough, I'm sick of your runny nose.
Come here...
527:
- What's going on?
- We're going to beat the rug.
528:
Listen, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I'm taking this off.
530:
I'll do my time and that's it. I'll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A watchman back at my collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532: I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or be a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the cap too!
Who's the Docent? A crook.
534:
- Crooks are many, but the cap is one.
- If we got the helmet, they'd cut our time.
535: Where'd he put it? We seem to have checked everything.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I had a runny nose?
And you: Jaws, jaws.
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they grabbed us. Remember, he says,
I'm fishing, and you go dive.
539:
- Wait, what did he say about fish then?
- I was fishing in an ice hole,
540:
- and you, he says, Squinty, can you swim?
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that's what!
541:
Exactly! I remember, bad person!
In the ice hole, in Malakhovka!
542:
Why'd you keep quiet? Jerk! You could've at least left a note when you were hanging yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- And him?
- Nothing. Let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let's go!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's there, at the bottom. Need to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—right away Squinty.
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold, I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now he was hanging himself, and now he's afraid of catching a cold!
- Fitness greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd stitch you up, but no time to fuss!
552:
Now it's two pieces.
And there's one more at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
